statement: The ocentra-enforcer MCP tools (coordination_claim, coordination_mail) refused to write with `writeCompatible:false, reloadRequired:true` because the long-running MCP process's loaded coordination code predates a git pull that touched src/coordination/{api,runner}.mjs on disk (a `package.json` byte-length delta was the tripwire). It returned a full `fallback.enforcerRunArguments` payload with the exact CLI invocation to use instead, and that fallback worked immediately.
why: This is EXECUTION_MODEL.md section 4's documented fail-closed guard working as designed (no mixed-version ledger writes), not a bug -- but a worker hitting it cold has no a priori reason to expect the MCP write tools to be unusable while the MCP read tools (ocentra_enforcer_check) keep working fine. The failure mode is asymmetric: reads silently work, writes hard-refuse.
howToApply: On ANY ocentra_enforcer_coordination_claim/mail/closeout MCP call that returns `ok:false` with `reloadRequired:true`, immediately use the `fallback.enforcerRunArguments`/`fallback.commandLine` field in the SAME error payload rather than retrying the MCP call or escalating -- it is a ready-to-run CLI command, not a diagnostic dead end.

evidence.ref: ocentra_enforcer_coordination_claim error payload, mcpFreshness.changedFiles: package.json byte delta 5282->5791

statement: The coordination fallback CLI (scripts/rust-rules.mjs) has no `mail` subcommand -- the actual command is `coordination message --to <lane> --body ...`. It also mis-parses some flag combinations: a claim/message call with `--hub <name>` before other flags produced an event whose own `hub` field was literally the string `"--lane"`, and one call ended up attributed to lane `orchestrator-wiretest` instead of the `--lane b04` I passed, even though the `to`/paths/reason fields were all correct.
why: The CLI's arg parser has an existing quirk (separate from the MCP staleness gate) where hub-name positional/flag resolution can bleed across flags depending on ordering; the resulting HubEvent is still structurally valid and delivered to the right recipient/paths, so the miswritten `hub`/`lane` display fields are cosmetic-ledger noise, not a delivery failure -- but a worker reading its own emitted event back would see the wrong hub/lane name and could wrongly conclude the send failed or went to the wrong lane.
howToApply: After any `coordination claim`/`message` fallback-CLI call, verify success via the `ok:true` field and the `paths`/`to`/`reason` fields specifically, not the `event.hub`/`event.lane` echo fields, which can be corrupted by flag-order parsing quirks in this CLI version. Do not resend/retry solely because the echoed hub/lane looks wrong.

evidence.ref: coordination claim response event.hub == "--lane"; message response lane == "orchestrator-wiretest" instead of b04

statement: arc-16's own module doc (crates/enforcer-coordination/src/lib.rs) explicitly defers the `enforcer coordination lane new/park/rm` worktree-spawn primitive AND the full `session`/`guard` orchestration surfaces -- but the b04 workpack text requires 'Default each assigned lane to its OWN worktree via arc-16's lane-worktree spawn primitive' as if that primitive already exists.
why: A workpack's Requirement Checklist can describe the TARGET shape (per EXECUTION_MODEL section 2b/3a) ahead of the dependency crate actually shipping the primitive it names; treating the checklist line as 'call arc-16's function X' literally would have blocked b04 entirely on an arc-16 gap that is explicitly out of MY owns scope to fill.
howToApply: When a workpack's checklist names a specific primitive from a dependency crate and that crate's own module doc marks it 'deferred', do not block or silently skip the requirement -- introduce a narrow trait/seam (here: `WorktreeSpawner`) that captures the REQUIRED behavior (default every lane to its own worktree, observably, under test) and that the real deferred primitive can satisfy later with zero call-site changes. Note the seam explicitly in both the code doc and here so a future arc-16 landing knows where to plug in.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-coordination/src/lib.rs Scope-of-this-pass section lists the lane worktree-spawn primitive under Deferred; crates/enforcer-plan/src/orchestrator.rs WorktreeSpawner trait + RecordingWorktreeSpawner

statement: ocentra_enforcer_check no-test-doubles (TEST-1.1) flags this module's FakeCoordination/ScriptedLiveness as forbidden mock/fake vocabulary, but the b04 workpack's own Acceptance-And-Proof text explicitly REQUIRES 'a claim/guard test uses an enforcer-coordination fake/in-memory harness' -- a direct conflict between a general-purpose lint and an explicit, named workpack requirement.
why: TEST-1.1 exists to stop tests from faking away the real behavior they should exercise, but the workpack's own design intentionally factors the coordination call contract behind a trait (CoordinationPort) specifically so a fast in-memory double and the real arc-16-backed implementation share identical tests -- this is the trait-seam pattern the rule is not written to distinguish from a lazy mock.
howToApply: Do not silently rename FakeCoordination to dodge the keyword scanner. Report the conflict explicitly (as here) so whoever owns the no-test-doubles rule definition can either scope an allow for CoordinationPort-shaped trait doubles, or the plan doctrine can record an explicit named exception for workpacks whose acceptance criteria mandate a fake/in-memory harness.

evidence.ref: rust-rules check no-test-doubles --files crates/enforcer-plan/src/orchestrator.rs: TEST-1.1 x 18 on FakeCoordination/ScriptedLiveness
